answer: Replay records the Python version and platform string in the run provenance, alongside the engine name/version and deterministic flag, model and scenario SHA-256, seed base and replication count, input hash, invocation, metrics/convergence/uncertainty/sensitivity, and a result hash. The environment archive is bounded: there is no full environment lock, container image, dependency lock or complete artifact archive, so a library or platform change can still alter behavior. The stored platform and Python strings only make a cross-environment difference visible. They do not guarantee bit-identical behavior across platforms: replay proves the stored inputs, engine version and seed reproduce the stored metrics on the same platform family, not that another platform will produce bit-identical floats, and presenting a one-platform replay as a guarantee for every platform is the cross-platform overclaim failure mode.
